title: Materials
sub: Basic, Lambert, Standard, and why everything is black
cards/0/title: A material is how a surface looks
cards/0/body:
MeshBasicMaterial: a flat fill that ignores light.
MeshLambertMaterial: matte, cheap, reacts to light.
MeshStandardMaterial: physically based (PBR), with roughness and metalness. The de facto standard, same as in glTF.
cards/1/task: MeshStandardMaterial, yet all you see is a black silhouette. Fix it with light.
cards/2/q: Why is MeshStandardMaterial black without light?
cards/2/options/0: It computes how much light the surface reflects; no light, nothing to reflect
cards/2/explain: The most common beginner mistake: "I see nothing" even though the camera is fine.
cards/3/task: There is light, but the knot looks flat, with no depth. Change the material.
cards/4/body:
roughness: 0 is mirror smooth, 1 is matte (the default is 1).
metalness: 0 is plastic, wood, stone; 1 is metal.

Metal needs something to reflect: without an environment map (scene.environment) it looks dark. That is an intermediate-level topic.
cards/5/q: Match each material to its use
cards/6/q: Which materials react to light? Select all that apply.
cards/6/explain: Physical is an extended Standard: clearcoat, glass, fabric.
cards/7/explain: shininess belongs to Phong, not Standard.
